The '''Ministry of Transport Rescue and Salvage Bureau of the People's Republic of China''' (中华人民共和国交通运输部救助打捞局) (short form, '''China Rescue and Salvage''') is an institution directly under the [[Ministry of Transport of the People's Republic of China]]. It is the most important [[maritime rescue]] and [[Marine salvage|salvage]] organization in China, and the only one that operates at national level. It is based in Beijing.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Rescue |first1=China |last2=Rescue |first2=Salvage Bureau China |title=China Rescue & Salvage Bureau » Membership – The International Salvage Union – Saving Lives, Ships and Cargo |url=https://www.marine-salvage.com/membership/name/china-rescue-salvage-company/ |access-date=2024-06-08 |language=en-GB |archive-date=2024-06-08 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240608204125/https://www.marine-salvage.com/membership/name/china-rescue-salvage-company/ |url-status=live }}</ref> As of 2022, it had 10,000 employees, 80% of whom were professional technical personnel, divers, and crew, manning 191 vessels (76 specialist rescue vessels, and 132 specialist salvage vessels), 20 rescue aircraft and 21 specialist rescue teams.<ref name=":1" />

CRS has gained a good international reputation for its willingness and ability to operate in extreme bad sea conditions,<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last1=Erickson |first1=Andrew S. |last2=Hickey |first2=Joshua |last3=Holst |first3=Henry |date=Spring 2019 |title=Surging Second Sea Force: China's Maritime Law-Enforcement Forces, Capabilities, and Future in the Gray Zone and Beyond |url=https://digital-commons.usnwc.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=7971&context=nwc-review |url-status=live |journal=Naval War College Review |volume=72 |issue=2 |pages=24 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230805205115/https://digital-commons.usnwc.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=7971&context=nwc-review |archive-date=2023-08-05 |access-date=2024-06-07}}</ref> receiving a number of international prizes.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-09-17 |title=IMRF Awards 2021 - Captain Chen Jian, China Rescue & Salvage (CRS) |url=https://www.international-maritime-rescue.org/news/imrf-awards-2021-captain-chen-jian-china-rescue-salvage-crs |access-date=2024-06-08 |website=International Maritime Rescue Federation |language=en |archive-date=2024-06-08 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240608204125/https://www.international-maritime-rescue.org/news/imrf-awards-2021-captain-chen-jian-china-rescue-salvage-crs |url-status=live }}</ref> The CRS also engages in commercial salvage work, and other forms of marine engineering.

==History==
The origin of China Rescue and Salvage are in a series of local institutions based in Shanghai. In 1951, with the approval of the [[Central People's Government]], the [[Central Ministry of Communications]] decided to merge the Maritime (Salvage) Department of the State-owned Maritime Transport Bureau with the nationalized Huaxing Salvage Company.<ref>{{Cite web |title=招商局集团与交通运输部救捞局签署战略合作框架协议－国务院国有资产监督管理委员会 |url=http://www.sasac.gov.cn/n2588025/n2588124/c4122592/content.html |access-date=2024-06-11 |website=www.sasac.gov.cn |archive-date=2024-06-12 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240612001939/http://www.sasac.gov.cn/n2588025/n2588124/c4122592/content.html |url-status=live }}</ref> On 24 August 1951, a new state-owned enterprise, the '''Chinese People's Salvage Company''' was established in [[Shanghai]], responsible for navigation and salvage at the [[Huangpu River]] and [[Yangtze River]] estuaries. The company had to deal with 59 shipwrecks at the bottom of the Huangpu River that had sunk from the end of 1948 to the beginning of 1949 (during the [[Chinese Civil War]]), and with hundreds of shipwrecks in the Yangtze River estuary channel, by sealing holed hulls and pumping water, mud removal, [[barge]] lifting, shipwreck removal, and channel dredging. The company had 120 employees, including 6 members of the [[Chinese Communist Party]].<ref name=":5" />

On 4 November 1952, [[Chen Yun]], director of the Financial and Economic Committee of the Central People's Government Administration Council, issued Public License No. 243 to the China People's Salvage Company. At that time, the company had only one 125-kilowatt [[tugboat|tug]] (the ''Panshan''—盘山号) and more than ten small barges.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.shtong.gov.cn/newsite/node2/node2245/node70962/node70972/index.html |title=《上海救捞志》第六章救捞机构、企业 第一节交通部上海海上救助打捞局 |access-date=2022-07-09 |archive-date=2019-02-27 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190227064959/http://www.shtong.gov.cn/newsite/node2/node2245/node70962/node70972/index.html |url-status=live }}</ref> In four years, the company managed to remove 104 wrecks of around 100,000 tons total [[Displacement (ship)|displacement]], mostly from the Huangpu and [[Yangtze delta]].<ref name="【中国救捞与远洋拖航】_信德海事网-专业海事信息咨询服务平台">{{Cite web |title=【中国救捞与远洋拖航】_信德海事网-专业海事信息咨询服务平台 |url=https://www.xindemarinenews.com/m/view.php?aid=3722 |access-date=2024-06-11 |website=www.xindemarinenews.com |archive-date=2024-06-12 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240612001847/https://www.xindemarinenews.com/m/view.php?aid=3722 |url-status=live }}</ref> From 12 February 1953, the Chinese People's Salvage Company used the name "Salvage Company of the General Administration of Navigation Engineering". [[Zhang Zhikui]] served as the manager from August 1953 until January 1966.<ref>[https://epaper.gmw.cn/gmrb/html/1985-08/22/nw.D110000gmrb_19850822_1-02.htm 本报特派记者　李树喜：“‘掘海人’的追求——记潜水打捞专家张智魁”，《光明日报》1985年08月22日星期四02版]{{Dead link|date=June 2024 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> From 1 January 1956, the company's name changed to "Salvage Engineering Bureau of the General Administration of Navigation Engineering", still with the nature of a business institution. On 1 July 1958, it was renamed Shanghai Salvage Engineering Bureau.{{Citation needed|date=March 2025}}

On 23 July 1958, the then Minister of Transportation [[Wang Shoudao]] ordered the merging of maritime rescue with salvage operations. From 16 September 1958, shipwrecks in the coastal waters of China from [[Wenzhou]] to the mouth of the [[Yalu River]] were placed under the responsibility of the Shanghai Salvage Engineering Bureau, making the SSEB into the first national-level combined rescue and salvage organization. The SSEB first set up three rescue stations at [[Yantai]], Shanghai, and [[Wenzhou]]. On 15 February 1963, the Shanghai Salvage Engineering Bureau was renamed the Shanghai Maritime Rescue and Salvage Bureau. In December 1963, the Ministry of Communications set up the Yantai Rescue Station and the Tianjin Rescue Station as detached units.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=历史沿革-交通运输部烟台打捞局 |url=https://www.ytsalvage.com/about/history.htm |access-date=2024-06-11 |website=www.ytsalvage.com |archive-date=2024-05-11 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240511041945/https://www.ytsalvage.com/about/history.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> By the first half of 1964, five rescue stations had been built in [[Tianjin]], Yantai, Shanghai, Wenzhou, and [[Xiamen]].<ref name="【中国救捞与远洋拖航】_信德海事网-专业海事信息咨询服务平台"/>
A major inciting incident for the development of Chinese maritime rescue occurred on 9 October 1973, when the Greek freighter ''Baltic Klif'' sank<ref>{{Cite web |last=FLEET WEATHER CENTRAL/JOINT TYPHOON WARNING CENTER |first=Guam, Mariana Islands |title=Annual Typhoon Report 1973 |url=https://apps.dtic.mil/sti/tr/pdf/ADA399669.pdf |access-date=2024-06-11 |website=Defense Technical Information Center (DTIC) |page=40 |archive-date=2024-06-12 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240612001840/https://apps.dtic.mil/sti/tr/pdf/ADA399669.pdf |url-status=live }}</ref> outside of [[Fujian]] province during [[Typhoon Nora (1973)|Typhoon Nora]]<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://zhuanlan.zhihu.com/p/361734640 |access-date=2024-06-08 |website=zhuanlan.zhihu.com |title=Archived copy |archive-date=2024-06-08 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240608204127/https://zhuanlan.zhihu.com/p/361734640 |url-status=live }}</ref> without effective response by the Chinese authorities of the port of Xiamen,<ref>{{Cite web |title=美国海空军共计入侵中国领海领空500余次 终于摸清了_资讯_凤凰网 |url=https://news.ifeng.com/world/3/200806/0624_2592_614481.shtml |access-date=2024-06-11 |website=news.ifeng.com |archive-date=2008-06-27 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080627163050/http://news.ifeng.com/world/3/200806/0624_2592_614481.shtml |url-status=live }}</ref> which made [[Zhou Enlai]] complain about the "cowardice" of the slow reaction. This extremely sharp rebuke (in the middle of the [[Cultural Revolution]], when such rebukes tended to have dangerous outcomes) caused a drive to strengthen coastal rescue networks across the country.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.shtong.gov.cn/newsite/node2/node2245/node70962/node70977/node71005/userobject1ai75019.html |title=《上海救捞志》 第十一章专记 第四节"波罗的海克里夫"号沉船事件 |accessdate=2020-11-17 |archive-date=2016-04-25 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160425115634/http://www.shtong.gov.cn/Newsite/node2/node2245/node70962/node70977/node71005/userobject1ai75019.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

As a reaction, in 1973 the [[State Council of the People's Republic of China|State Council]] and the [[Central Military Commission (China)|Central Military Commission]] jointly issued a document to establish the National Maritime Security Command. In 1974, a national maritime search and rescue work conference was held in [[Qingdao]]. The meeting decided that the Ministry of Transport would establish two new maritime security headquarters in [[Yantai]] and [[Guangzhou]]. The Guangzhou Maritime Rescue and Salvage Bureau (the former Third Engineering Team of China People's Salvage Company) was created that same year, and on 28 September 1974, the Yantai Shipwreck Rescue and Salvage Bureau of the Ministry of Transport was officially established. On 30 April 1975, the [[Tianjin]] and Yantai rescue stations were formally transferred to the Yantai Salvage Bureau, and 308 employees, 3 tugboats, 3 salvage barges, 20 salvage [[buoy]]s, and total assets of 130,000 yuan were transferred with them.<ref>{{Cite web |title=单位简介-交通运输部烟台打捞局 |url=https://www.ytsalvage.com/about/about.htm? |access-date=2024-06-11 |website=www.ytsalvage.com |archive-date=2024-05-11 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240511042036/https://www.ytsalvage.com/about/about.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

The three new Salvage Bureaus started building 9 rescue stations, built rescue docks, radio stations, and recruited [[People's Liberation Army Navy]] veterans to expand their force.'''<ref name="【中国救捞与远洋拖航】_信德海事网-专业海事信息咨询服务平台"/> '''The bureaus also started to add high-horsepower, specialized rescue tugs. In 1975, China bought from Japan its first purpose-built deep-sea rescue tug, the ''Hujiu 101'' (沪救101号, literally ''Shanghai Rescue 101''), a {{cvt|87|m|ftin}} long, {{cvt|14|m|ftin}} [[Beam (nautical)|beam]], and 2,100 tons displacement vessel.'''<ref>{{Cite web|title=|url=http://www.zhushiyao.com/?tag=%E5%8D%97%E6%B5%B7On}}{{Dead link|date=December 2024 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.safechina.cn/anli/huozai/2010-12-07/752.html |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120911202933/http://www.safechina.cn/anli/huozai/2010-12-07/752.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=September 11, 2012 |title=沪救101"号轮拖主机意外飞车 导致船舶大火 |date=2010-12-03 |accessdate=2012-05-03 }}</ref> '''
Soon after, with the start of the [[reform and opening]], the bureaus were also progressively allowed to operate commercially, the Shanghai bureau under the name "Shanghai Tug Company". With the rapid growth of marine traffic as China foreign trade grew, the opportunities for profitable activities became common, and as the Bureaus were allowed to retain earnings for reinvestment, they grew steadily in equipment and capabilities.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |date=2021-08-24 |title=交通运输部救助打捞局成立70周年 海上救助8.2万人 |url=https://www.workercn.cn/c/2021-08-24/6907045.shtml |access-date=2024-06-12 |website=The Worker |archive-date=2024-06-12 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240612001845/https://www.workercn.cn/c/2021-08-24/6907045.shtml |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name=":3" />

As part of the generalized reform for the commercialization of [[State-owned enterprises of China|SOEs]], on 28 February 2003, the Ministry of Communications, the National Development and Reform Commission, and six other ministries and commissions jointly issued the "Notice on Issuing the Implementation Plan for the Salvage and Rescue System Reform" (Jiao Ren Lao Fa [2003] No. 60), formally implementing a wide reform of the salvage and rescue system. Starting on 1 April 2003, the Ministry of Transport implemented this reform, separating rescue from salvage. The three salvage bureaus allocated assets to three new Maritime Rescue Bureaus, in the Beihai (Northern Seas—[[Yellow Sea|Yellow]] and [[Bohai Sea|Bohai]] seas), Donghai ([[East China Sea]]), and Nanhai ([[South China Sea]]), co-located but separate from the three salvage bureaus in Yantai, Shanghai, and Guangzhou. Four rescue aviation squadrons were also raised.<ref name=":3"/>

The logic of the reform was that while rescue duties are part of the peremptory public service of protecting life, ship salvage is not as time sensitive and, when not involving urgent seaway clearance, can be made into a commercial activity. After the split, the salvage bureaus would some carry out some emergency duties such as disaster relief and urgent salvage operations, while also engage in commercial salvage of sunken ships and sunken objects in public waterways; port debris clearance; rescue and salvage of distressed ships where there is no risk to life; emergency emptying of [[Heavy fuel oil|bunker]] from sunken ships, and containment of oil spills from distressed ships; and prevention of environmental pollution resulting from marine accidents.<ref name=":3" /> It was expected they would use their profits to fund equipment and preparation for both the salvage and the rescue units.

The new six bureaus were put under the vertical leadership of the '''Rescue and Salvage Bureau of the Ministry of Transport''', which coordinates their activities, although all six subordinate bureaus operate autonomously.<ref>{{Cite web |title=《中国交通部四月起将确立救助、打捞新体制》，中国新闻网，2003-03-08 |url=http://news.sohu.com/52/12/news206921252.shtml |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050224121131/http://news.sohu.com/52/12/news206921252.shtml |archive-date=2005-02-24 |access-date=2022-06-09}}</ref> The CSR in its various incarnations has, in the period between 24 August 1951 to 23 August 2021, rescued a total of 82,783 people (12,703 foreigners) and 5,424 ships in distress (957 foreign ships) in harsh sea conditions and other emergency and dangerous environments, and salvaged 1,827 sunken ships (99 foreign ships).<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021 |title=单位简介 |url=http://www.crsmot.org.cn/jigougk_jlj/danweijj_jjgk/ |website=China Rescue and Salvage Bureau Website }}{{Dead link|date=June 2024 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref><ref name=":4" /> Since the 2003 reform, the Guangzhou Bureaus have carried out a total of 423 salvage missions, rescued 129 ships, and rescued property worth RMB 7.08 billion; salvaged 59 sunken ships, recovered 185 bodies of victims, and rescued 1,133 people;<ref>{{Cite web|title=单位概况|url=http://www.gz-salvage.com.cn/index.php?ac=article&at=list&tid=2|access-date=2024-06-11|website=Guangzhou Salvage Bureau|archive-date=2020-08-02|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200802122301/http://gz-salvage.com.cn/index.php?ac=article&at=list&tid=2|url-status=live}}</ref> the Shanghai bureaus; and the Yantai bureaus have carried out 512 salvage missions, rescued 3,163 people, salvaged 183 sunken ships, and recovered 5,000 tons of spilled oil.<ref name=":3" />

==Functions==

China Rescue and Salvage is by law responsible for emergency response to maritime emergencies in Chinese waters, including life saving operations, ship and property rescue, shipwreck and sunken object salvage, maritime firefighting, cleanup of oil spills, and other public welfare responsibilities such as providing safety guarantee for maritime transportation and offshore resource developments. Its Chinese motto is "three rescues and one salvage" (i.e. human life rescue, environmental rescue, property rescue, and emergency salvage).<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=单位简介 |url=http://www.crsmot.org.cn/jigougk_jlj/danweijj_jjgk/ |access-date=2024-06-09 |website=China Rescue and Salvage Bureau }}{{Dead link|date=June 2024 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

The CRS has some policy-making obligations as well, preparing the five-year-plans for the national salvage system,<ref>{{Cite web |title=深入实施救捞系统"十四五"发展规划，加快推进现代化专业救捞体系建设——《救捞系统"十四五"发展规划》解读-2022年在线访谈-中华人民共和国交通运输部 |url=https://www.mot.gov.cn/zxft2022/jiulaofz/ |access-date=2024-06-11 |website=www.mot.gov.cn}}</ref> and some administrative duties such as coordinating maritime air patrols, and taking command and coordination roles of major rescue and salvage operations. It also has the duty to fulfill some of China's international obligations (such as some China's [[SOLAS Convention|SOLAS obligations]]). The CRS must also collect the data and statistics related to rescue operations and salvage in China,<ref name=":2" />{{efn| The ultimate legal obligation of guaranteeing life and traffic safety in Chinese waters falls on the [[China Maritime Safety Administration|CMSA]] and its subordinate Maritime Search and Rescue Center, the CRS is the "specialist" rescue agency, the most active and well-equipped of the various maritime agencies and salvage companies in the country, and must legally "take point" in rescue and salvage operations, but both the CMSA and the [[China Coast Guard]] ships have rescue obligations as well.}}
CRS cooperates very closely with the [[China Maritime Safety Administration]]'s [[China Maritime Search and Rescue Center|Maritime Search and Rescue Center]] (中国海上搜救中心), which is the main maritime SAR coordinator in China, and with other emergency control centers in the country.<ref>{{Cite web |title=孕妇在外伶仃岛旅游突发羊水破裂，珠海组织紧急救援_腾讯新闻 |url=https://new.qq.com/rain/a/20240103A052QH00 |access-date=2024-06-11 |website=new.qq.com|date=3 January 2024 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-09-02 |title=关于协调救助"琼临高11055"轮 一名落水渔民的情况报告 |url=https://www.hn.msa.gov.cn/hsfw_7_2/41124.jhtml |access-date=2024-06-11 |website=www.hn.msa.gov.cn |archive-date=2023-09-24 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230924094837/https://www.hn.msa.gov.cn/hsfw_7_2/41124.jhtml |url-status=live }}</ref>

The various subordinate units of the CRS operate as commercial businesses as well, in particular the Shanghai Salvage Bureau, which with the name of China Offshore Engineering Solutions (COES) operates several national international subsidiaries, carrying out both salvage (such as the difficult lifting of the wreck of the [[ferry]] ''[[Sinking of MV Sewol|Sewol]]'' in one piece)<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-01-29 |title=让中国打捞技术走在世界前列——记"国家卓越工程师团队"交通运输部上海打捞局救捞工程关键技术攻关团队 |url=http://www.zgsyb.com/news.html?aid=673593 |access-date=2024-06-11 |website=www.zgsyb.com}}</ref> and other marine engineering operations (such as long-distance towing the [[aircraft carrier]] {{ship|Soviet aircraft carrier|Kiev||2}},<ref>{{Cite web |title=History-COES |url=https://www.coes.cn/en/about/history/index.html |access-date=2024-06-11 |website=www.coes.cn |archive-date=2024-06-12 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240612002411/https://www.coes.cn/en/about/history/index.html |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Caisson (engineering)|caisson]] and [[immersed tunnel]] placement,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Company Profile |url=https://www.coescaledonia.com/company-profile/ |access-date=2024-06-11 |website=COES Caledonia |language=en-GB |archive-date=2023-12-09 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231209092731/https://www.coescaledonia.com/company-profile/ |url-status=live }}</ref> and even [[underwater archeology]].)<ref>{{Cite web |title=历史沿革-交通运输部上海打捞局 |url=https://www.coes.cn/about/history/index.html |access-date=2024-06-11 |website=www.coes.cn |archive-date=2024-06-12 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240612002412/https://www.coes.cn/about/history/index.html |url-status=live }}</ref> The other salvage bureaus also operate underwater engineering, land reclamation, ship repair, shipbuilding, and harbor engineering companies.<ref>{{Cite web |title=港航工程中心 |url=http://www.gz-salvage.com.cn/index.php?ac=article&at=read&did=64 |access-date=2024-06-11 ==Organization==


===Internal units===
Source:<ref>{{Cite web |title=机构设置 |url=http://www.crsmot.org.cn/jigougk_jlj/jigousz_jggk/ |access-date=2024-06-09 |website=China Rescue and Salvage Bureau }}{{Dead link|date=June 2024 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

#'''General Office''' (办公室): General management, confidentiality and international affairs.  
#'''Planning, Construction, and Science and Technology Office''' (规划建设科技处): Responsible for equipment acquisition, compliance with industry standards, statistics and information work.    
#'''Finance Office''' (财务处) Budget management. 
#'''Personnel and Education Office''' (人事e 处) Personnel education and training, technical cadre management. Certification of divers and other specialists.
#'''Rescue Management Office''' (救助管理处): coordinate the on-call rescue forces, life, environmental, and military rescue duties. Responsible for units readiness.
#'''Aviation Management Office''' (飞行管理处) Responsible for the leadership and management of the maritime rescue flight teams of the Rescue and Salvage Bureau of the Ministry of Transport; responsible for the team building and air and ground safety management of the maritime rescue flight team; responsible for the command, dispatch and coordination of maritime rescue flights.    
#'''Salvage Management Office''' (打捞管理处): Responsible for salvage business management, manage the affiliated salvage companies.  
#'''Safety Supervision and Management Office''' (安全监督管理处): Responsible for the comprehensive safety management and accident handling of the entire salvage system.   
#'''Audit Office''' (审计处): Auditing and asset management.  
#'''Party and Mass Work Office''' (Organization Office) 党群工作处（组织处）Party work, organization and management of cadres, and publicity.  
#'''Office of the Discipline Inspection Commission''' (纪委办公室) Supervision and discipline.

=== Subordinate units ===
As of 2021, the CRS had a total of 24 rescue bases, 88 rescue ship standby points (coastal and at sea), 10 rescue flight airbases, and 115 temporary take-off/landing points (for helicopters)<ref name=":4" /> spread in the coastline between the Yalu River in the north to the South China Sea Islands in the south.<ref>{{Cite web |title=中国航海学会救助打捞专业委员会 |url=http://www.china-salvage.cn/hydw.asp |access-date=2024-06-08 |website=www.china-salvage.cn |archive-date=2024-06-08 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240608205138/http://www.china-salvage.cn/hydw.asp |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=中国海上应急抢验救助打捞急救 |url=https://www.transportation.gov/sites/dot.gov/files/docs/5.search%20and%20rescue(chs).pdf |access-date=2024-06-09 |archive-date=2024-06-08 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240608205149/https://www.transportation.gov/sites/dot.gov/files/docs/5.search%20and%20rescue(chs).pdf |url-status=live }}</ref> Its subordinate units are as follows:

== China Rescue and Salvage Exhibition Hall (中国救捞陈列馆) ==
The China Salvage Exhibition Hall was established in 2011, located in the Sea Rescue Building, No. 1426, Yangshupu Road, Shanghai. The exhibition hall covers an area of 1,636 square meters with general exhibits of salvage equipment, models, multimedia presentations, etc. The museum is open free of charge from August 2018.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2011-08-23 |title=国际海上人命救助联盟亚太中心8月23日在沪成立 |url=http://www.gov.cn/jrzg/2011-08/23/content_1930996.htm |website= |publisher=新华社 |access-date= |via=中国政府网 |archive-date=2022-07-09 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220709053445/http://www.gov.cn/jrzg/2011-08/23/content_1930996.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

extract:
The Ministry of Transport Rescue and Salvage Bureau of the People's Republic of China (中华人民共和国交通运输部救助打捞局) (short form, China Rescue and Salvage) is an institution directly under the Ministry of Transport of the People's Republic of China. It is the most important maritime rescue and salvage organization in China, and the only one that operates at national level. It is based in Beijing. As of 2022, it had 10,000 employees, 80% of whom were professional technical personnel, divers, and crew, manning 191 vessels (76 specialist rescue vessels, and 132 specialist salvage vessels), 20 rescue aircraft and 21 specialist rescue teams.
CRS has gained a good international reputation for its willingness and ability to operate in extreme bad sea conditions, receiving a number of international prizes. The CRS also engages in commercial salvage work, and other forms of marine engineering.
